week_in_brief: Inventory's still stuck, leads are expensive, and brokerages are starting to realize AI adoption metrics don't pay the bills.

items.headline: Portal Leads Are Broken — Build a Referral Engine Instead
items.whats_happening: Portal lead costs spiked post-NAR settlement and conversion rates remain dismal — real estate contact forms convert at 0.6%, the lowest of any industry, yet only 27% of those leads ever get contacted. Meanwhile, agents running relationship marketing programs are seeing 74% YoY growth with near-zero ad spend by focusing on past clients and referral engines.
items.so_what: Move budget away from Zillow volume buying and into systems that make it easy for agents to stay top-of-mind with past clients. Referrals and past clients convert faster and cost less than cold portal leads.

items.headline: AI Adoption Is High, Productivity Gains Are Not
items.whats_happening: Ninety-seven percent of brokerage leaders report agents using AI, and 82% of agents use AI for listing descriptions. But the gap between adoption and output is substantial — many agents hit those numbers using free public tools outside your approved stack, and per-agent productivity hasn't moved. License count is not the same as real productivity.
items.so_what: Measure actual output change, not adoption metrics. Run six-week productivity loops on high-value workflows to close the gap between tool usage and revenue impact. If 97% of your agents use AI but 70% produce the same volume as two years ago, the tools aren't the problem — the workflow is.

items.headline: Agentic AI Introduces New Fair Housing and MLS Compliance Risks
items.whats_happening: AI is shifting from tool-based (agent-controlled) to agentic (executes workflows autonomously). Agents are already experimenting with systems that can draft messages, update CRM records, and schedule follow-ups without human intervention. NAR's chief data officer flagged serious risks: MLS compliance violations, fair housing exposure from automated discriminatory patterns, and workflow delegation to unlicensed AI.
items.so_what: Establish human review checkpoints now and define approved tool suites before liability shows up. The risk window is closing — agents won't wait for perfect policies, and the first lawsuit will come from a workflow you didn't know was automated.

items.headline: Inventory Growth Is Still Stuck, and Sellers Still Have the Upper Hand
items.whats_happening: Inventory grew only 0.247% year-over-year last week, with three of the last four weeks showing negative YoY growth. NAR expects a modest H2 recovery if inventory expansion continues, but the floor is rising slowly, not roaring back. Sellers retain leverage, and agents can afford to be selective with lead quality rather than chasing volume.
items.so_what: Emphasize qualified-buyer outreach over volume. In markets where inventory still favors sellers, marketing should focus on readiness and relationship strength, not urgency campaigns that assume buyer desperation.

this_weeks_take: The brokerage that wins in 2026 isn't the one with the highest AI adoption rate — it's the one that turned adoption into actual productivity. Stop measuring tool usage and start measuring revenue per agent.
